econometric_drivers.title: Kenai Refining Island, ANS Feedstock & Arctic Volatility Dynamics
econometric_drivers.description: Alaska constitutes an isolated sub-arctic petroleum subsystem. The Marathon Kenai Refinery (68 kbpd) on Cook Inlet supplies Southcentral Alaska and the railbelt via pipeline and marine barges, running Alaska North Slope (ANS) and local Cook Inlet crude. Remote interior and bush communities rely on seasonal ice-free summer river barges and Alaska Railroad tank cars, governed by extreme sub-zero winter volatility blending requirements (15.0+ psi RVP).

refining_logistics.title: Marathon Kenai Refinery & Cook Inlet Marine Corridors
refining_logistics.description: Supply is anchored by the 68,000 bpd Marathon Kenai Refinery located on Cook Inlet, producing gasoline, jet fuel for international air cargo at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport, and ultra-low sulfur diesel. Refined products move across Cook Inlet to the Port of Alaska in Anchorage via marine tanker, barge, and pipeline.
pipelines: Alaska Railroad Railbelt Tank Car Line

tax_structure.title: Alaska Lowest U.S. Statutory Motor Fuel Excise Tax Burden
tax_structure.description: Alaska enforces the lowest state motor fuel excise tax in the nation at only $0.0895/gal. Combined with Federal excise ($0.184/gal), the statutory baseline burden is only $0.2735/gal, over 67 cents below California and 40 cents below Washington.
tax_structure.notes: Statutory baseline excise tax of $0.274/gal; lowest motor fuel tax burden in the United States.

infrastructure_delivery.title: Port of Alaska Terminal Margin & Railbelt Logistics
infrastructure_delivery.description: Anchorage rack prices reflect Kenai marine transit across Cook Inlet and terminal handling at the Port of Alaska, which processes over 85% of all refined fuel consumed in Southcentral and Interior Alaska.
infrastructure_delivery.hub_name: Port of Alaska Anchorage Marine Fuel Terminal & Kenai Dock

shock_scenarios.name: Cook Inlet Severe Sea Ice Marine Transit Suspension
shock_scenarios.subtitle: Winter Dynamic Sea Ice Stranding Fuel Tankers and Barges
shock_scenarios.description: Heavy pan ice in upper Cook Inlet halts barge movements into the Port of Alaska, threatening fuel reserves and requiring emergency highway trucking from Kenai.

shock_scenarios.name: Marathon Kenai Refinery Unplanned FCC Unit Outage
shock_scenarios.subtitle: Single-Refinery Alaskan Supply Shocks
shock_scenarios.description: Fluid catalytic cracker outage at Kenai reduces in-state production by 60%, necessitating costly waterborne marine imports from Puget Sound.

shock_scenarios.name: ANS Crude In-State Feedstock Surplus Discount
shock_scenarios.subtitle: Trans-Alaska Pipeline Supply Abundance Softening Costs
shock_scenarios.description: Increased North Slope crude availability depresses local feedstock acquisition costs at Cook Inlet refineries.
